name: Emily Ann Ramos
title: Mayor of Mountain View
years_of_service: Appointed to the Mountain View City Council in January 2023 to fill a vacancy (per scc-measure-e-2026.json, sourced to the Mountain View Voice and Council record); selected by her council peers as Mayor for a one-year term under the city's council-manager system, per Wikipedia's Mountain View, California article (citing Mountain View Voice, "Ramos picked as Mountain View's new mayor, Clark as vice mayor"). Mountain View's charter has the seven-member, at-large council elect the mayor and vice mayor from among themselves each year, so this profile cannot independently confirm from sources reviewed whether Ramos has since been re-elected to a full council term or reappointed mayor beyond that initial selection.
background: Ramos was appointed, not elected, to the Mountain View City Council in January 2023, when the Council chose to fill a vacancy by appointment rather than call a special election, citing the roughly $2.1 million cost of a special election; that decision drew public criticism from residents who argued it denied voters a say, a controversy documented in the Voter Information Guide analysis for Measure E (content/measures/scc-measure-e-2026.json), which Ramos, now Mayor, would extend the underlying decision window on. Her colleagues subsequently selected her as Mayor, with Chris Clark as Vice Mayor; the City Manager during her mayoralty is Kimbra McCarthy.

As Mayor, Ramos is the filer and lead signer of the primary argument in favor of Measure F, the November 2026 measure that would let the Mountain View City Council raise the city's Transient Occupancy Tax from 10% to as much as 15%; her argument states plainly that if voters approve it, the Council will decide the actual new rate at a public meeting after the election. She is also one of five signers, alongside Vice Mayor Chris Clark, Councilmember Lucas Ramirez, and two school-district trustees, of the primary argument in favor of Measure E, the City Charter modernization measure, which (among other things) would double the Council's vacancy-decision window from 30 to 60 days, the same process used to appoint her to the Council in 2023. Full detail on both measures is in content/measures/scc-measure-f-2026.json and content/measures/scc-measure-e-2026.json and is not duplicated here.

I was not able to independently verify Ramos's pre-council career, education, or occupation. WebSearch was unavailable (session budget exhausted) and direct WebFetch attempts at Mountain View's official city-council biography page (mountainview.gov) returned a 403 Forbidden; the only official-site detail obtained was via Wikipedia's citation of Mountain View Voice reporting. Because of that, committee_memberships, voting_record_highlights, endorsements_received, and past_measures_authored are left empty or minimal below rather than populated with unverified claims.
attendance: No individually published meeting-attendance or voting-participation record for Mayor Ramos was found in this session. Mountain View's council meetings and agendas run through a Legistar-based system (used elsewhere in this research, e.g. for Measure E and Measure F sourcing), which would in principle allow a manual attendance tally, but compiling one was not feasible within this session's tool budget; the city's own council-directory page could not be fetched (403 Forbidden).
